blindSummary: A penal-code provision criminalises "immodest or unnatural acts" (up to 3 years); recent enforcement evidence is limited but discrimination and violence are documented, and there is no legal gender recognition.
blindSourceSummaries: NOTE: not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying international legal-aid trust's country profile documents this country's criminalisation of same-sex activity (up to 3 years' imprisonment under the penal code).

An LGBTI human-rights organisation founded in 2007, with an international partner's alternative report (June 2021) to the UN Human Rights Committee's 132nd session: the organisation fights HIV among men who have sex with men in this country and documents human-rights violations here and in neighbouring states sharing its official language; provides legal and judicial support for victims, advocacy, capacity building.

A foreign government's 2023 human-rights report on this country: official assessment - same-sex conduct criminalised under a dedicated penal-code article; societal discrimination; no legal protections.
An LGBT community newspaper (Aug 2015): reportage on the experiences of LGBT members of the region's largest churches, including in this country.

A foreign government's 2011 human-rights report on this country: documents security-force torture, impunity, and 'official and societal discrimination... against members of the lesbian, gay, bisexual and transgender (LGBT) community'.

A foreign government's 2022 human-rights report on this country: significant issues include cruel treatment, harsh prisons, arbitrary detention, criminal libel enforcement, and 'crimes involving violence or threats of violence targeting lesbian, gay, bisexual...' persons.
blindTangential: "Immodest or unnatural acts" criminalised (3 years) — formal exposure for visitors travelling with partners.
